items.title: PostgreSQL@SCaLE24x CfP closing soon on Nov 1, 2027
items.summary: Hi folks!We're hosting a PostgreSQL track at SCaLE again — come join us in sunny Pasadena!PostgreSQL@SCaLE is a two-day event on Thursday–Friday, April 1–2, 2027, at the Pasadena Convention Center, part of SCaLE 24x (April 1–4).The program brings together PostgreSQL core contributors, long-time community leaders, and professionals running Postgres in production to share practical, experience-driven knowledge. Sessions cover how PostgreSQL works, how to operate it reliably at scale, and how to use it well in modern systems — from foundational operations through advanced internals and large-scale deployments.Who it's forDatabase administrators (DBAs)Backend, web, and full-stack developersSysadmins and site reliability engineersPlatform, cloud-native, and Kubernetes practitionersAnyone running PostgreSQL in production or at homeWhat to expectPostgreSQL training — one Thursday track dedicated to full-day training led by experienced PostgreSQL educators and practitioners.Technical talks — internals, performance, replication, reliability, tooling, and modern workloads including AI and cloud-native environments.Community engagement — direct access to contributors and experienced operators, including an Ask Me Anything (AMA) session.Call for PapersThe CfP is open through November 1, 2026.Tag your submission PostgreSQL so it's routed to the PostgreSQL@SCaLE committee.

items.title: Estuary Expands PostgreSQL CDC with Targeted Backfills and Scalable Discovery
items.summary: Estuary has released several updates to its PostgreSQL change data capture (CDC) connector focused on backfill recovery, discovery at scale, and schema-change detection.Targeted BackfillsPostgreSQL capture bindings now support an Additional Backfill Filter, allowing a SQL expression to be applied to backfill queries for an individual table.This can reduce the amount of data that needs to be re-read when only a subset of a large PostgreSQL table needs to be recovered or re-backfilled. For example, teams can use an indexed identifier or timestamp to limit the rows included in a recovery backfill.The filter affects backfills only. Ongoing PostgreSQL CDC continues to capture new changes independently of the filter.Because the SQL expression is applied directly to backfill queries, this is an advanced option and should be configured carefully. Changing the filter requires the affected binding to be backfilled again.Discovery Controls for Large PostgreSQL SchemasEstuary has also added PostgreSQL discovery filters that allow captures to control which tables are surfaced during connector discovery.Captures can now:include only selected PostgreSQL schemasexclude selected schemasdiscover tables using glob-based table patternsoptionally discover tables that are not yet included in the PostgreSQL publicationThese controls are useful for PostgreSQL environments with large numbers of schemas or tables where only part of the database should participate in a CDC pipeline.Table metadata discovery is also processed in smaller groups to improve reliability when working with databases containing large numbers of tables.Configurable RediscoveryPostgreSQL captures can now configure how frequently Estuary re-runs discovery while a capture is active.Rediscovery is used to detect changes such as newly added tables and schema updates. The default interval is 15 minutes and can be adjusted for environments that require faster or less frequent discovery.This gives PostgreSQL operators more control over the trade-off between schema-change detection latency and catalog-query activity.PostgreSQL CDC and BackfillsEstuary's PostgreSQL source connector uses logical replication to capture inserts, updates, and deletes from the PostgreSQL write-ahead log (WAL).When a new capture starts, Estuary can first backfill the existing contents of selected tables and then transition to ongoing CDC. The new backfill and discovery controls provide additional options for operating this process on large PostgreSQL environments and during recovery scenarios.The PostgreSQL CDC connector supports PostgreSQL 10.0 and later across self-hosted PostgreSQL and managed PostgreSQL services.DocumentationPostgreSQL CDC connector documentationBackfilling data and additional backfill filters

items.title: Oxynote: an open source internal wiki with live PostgreSQL query charts
items.summary: Oxynote is a new open-source (Apache-2.0) internal wiki for engineering teams. A page can include a chart that runs its own query against Prometheus, PostgreSQL, MySQL, or MariaDB right next to the explanatory text, and changes to important pages go through a draft, a diff, and approval, like a pull request.Internal docs go stale because people open them only when something breaks. Live data gives the team a reason to open a page every day, and pages read daily stay up to date.How it works with PostgreSQL:Live Metrics blocks run SQL against your PostgreSQL databases and show the result as a time series, bar chart or gauge.Queries can use Grafana-style macros such as $__timeFilter, $__timeGroup and $__timeFrom, so existing dashboard queries carry over.Oxynote only connects to read-only data sources: a role or database with default_transaction_read_only enabled, or a standby. Every session also runs in read-only mode.Oxynote stores its own data in PostgreSQL 18, which is embedded in the all-in-one Docker image.A typical use is a runbook that shows replication lag or slow query counts next to the steps for handling them, so the chart and its explanation are reviewed together.Oxynote is available from:Source and install instructionsLatest release

items.title: ReviveDB: Supabase backups restore-tested against the source schema
items.summary: ReviveDB backs up Supabase projects on Postgres 17 outside Supabase, and restores every database backup into a temporary PostgreSQL database before it counts as verified.The restore is compared with an inventory of the source: tables, rows, columns, constraints, indexes, sequences, views, functions, triggers, RLS policies, grants and extensions. Row counts alone miss a restore that loses a constraint or a policy.Each backup run uses its own short-lived, read-only Postgres role that also reads rows behind row-level security. The same recovery point holds Auth data, Storage files and Edge Functions.A recovery point restores into a new Supabase project, or into the original after a rehearsal on a copy. Free for one project: https://revivedb.dev
